title: adaptive-slo-hysteresis-and-quorum-token-sampling-for-noise-resilient-alerting
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: On high-cardinality workloads we observed a lot of alert noise from short-lived token cost spikes and flapping alerts. Existing sampling and alerting thresholds amplify noise for low-volume tenants and obscure real regressions for mid-volume workloads. This PR implements a combined approach: per-SLO hysteresis windows to reduce sensitivity to transient bursts, and a quorum-based token sampler that ensures sampled traces reflect cohort-level behavior rather than single outliers. Goals: 1) reduce alert flapping for transient token bursts; 2) preserve signal for sustained regressions; 3) keep downstream storage and index costs bounded with adaptive sampling; 4) expose tuning knobs in Console and a migration plan for existing alerts. Design summary: - Hysteresis controller: each SLO route maintains a small state machine (stable->warming->violated->recovering) with configurable enter/exit windows expressed in seconds and minimum sustained token-rate percent. The controller uses exponentially-weighted windows to avoid hard re-eval cadence. - Quorum token sampler: instead of per-invocation independent sampling, the sampler groups recent invocations by route+tenant+prompt-shape window and applies a quorum rule (sample when >=N invocations in window OR when median token cost exceeds X percentile). Quorum threshold is adaptive based on tenant volume (low-volume tenants can use a lower quorum to retain signal). - Integration: the sampler tags traces with sampling_reason and quorum_id; the alert pipeline consumes those tags and performs quorum-aware aggregation for alert evaluation and incident grouping. - Backcompat: defaults preserve current sampling rates; behavior opt-in via a feature flag and cluster-wide rollout plan described in docs. Implementation highlights: - New package src/observability/sampling/quorum_sampler.rs implements the grouping index, quorum heuristics, and TTL eviction; heavy use of probabilistic reservoir sketches to keep memory bounded. - Alerts middleware telemetry/alerts/hysteresis.go adds SLO lifecycle state and emits state_transition spans to tracing. - Console doc docs/observability/token-sampling.md documents knobs and recommended defaults. - Helm chart value changes infra/helm/values.yaml add feature flag and tunables. - Tests: tests/sampling/integration_test.go covers behavior across volume tiers; loadbench results included below. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed with SREs and Console PM - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan included - [x] Performance bench and memory check Results and rationale: - On a synthetic mixed workload (10k tenants, Pareto distribution), average alert count per hour dropped by 46% for routes with high short-lived bursts; true positive detection latency for sustained regressions remained within 5% of baseline. - Quorum sampler memory budget measured ~0.9MB per 10k active route-tenants (within our budgets); CPU overhead on sampling path measured +3.2% p90. - Uncovered and fixed an edge-case where very low-volume tenants would never sample; added adaptive floor to quorum threshold. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable in staging for top-10 noisy routes; 2) 1% of production traffic with realtime dashboard; 3) 25% ramp after 48h, 100% after verification. Metrics to watch: alert-frequency, alert-flapping-rate, sampled-trace-rate, sampler-memory-usage, slo-state-transition-rate. Migration: existing alerts that use raw per-invocation counts should be migrated to quorum-aware aggregates; migration helper CLI in tools/obs-migrate included.

feat(alerts): add SLO hysteresis controller and transition tracing
